classification.difficultyReason: Form a similar-triangle relationship and apply the chain rule to connected lengths.

content.prompt:
A streetlight is on top of an 8 metre pole. A child $1.2\text{ m}$ tall walks away from the pole at $1\text{ m/s}$.

Find the rate at which the length of the shadow is changing.

spec.description: Pole on the left, child between pole and shadow tip, with ground segments x and s and their explanatory captions. The schematic is not to scale.
spec.mathematics: The small shadow triangle and complete light-ray triangle are similar; their bases are s and x+s.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is supplied in the question.

answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the shadow length and $x$ the distance between the child and the pole. Using similar triangles,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{s}{s+x}&=\frac{1.2}{8}\\8s&=1.2s+1.2x\\6.8s&=1.2x\\s&=\frac{3x}{17}\\\frac{ds}{dx}&=\frac{3}{17}.\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{ds}{dt}&=\frac{ds}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=\frac{3}{17}(1)\\&=\frac{3}{17}\text{ m/s}.\end{aligned}$$
